kind: CP2 — pilot/mid-work adversarial checkpoint (contract §1): what the measurements did to the design
filedAtBasis: Same single clock reading as CP1 (see CP1.filedAtBasis).
filedLate: Same disclosure as CP1: filed at close. The measurements below are read-backs from the staging store and the factory replica between 2026-09-17T16:00:28Z and 16:10:33Z; the reversal in 'theReversal' was made when q14 landed (16:09:15Z), before any code was written.

theReversal.whatTheDispatchExpected: Reading (a) as written in A-207: 'the served count includes the retired R-prefixed rows, which this bake will not rewrite, so the denominator is inflated by a population the source side never sees.'
theReversal.whatTheRowsShow: The R-prefixed served rows are NOT a population the source side never sees — they are the source's OWN id keyspace, and 282,569 of them are literally the same ids (q18: served R ids 282,569, source R ids 282,569, shared 282,569). The population the source table never keys is the NUMERIC one: txgio_parcel holds 0 numeric prop_ids for 48491, and the metric served set holds 319,480 numeric rows of which 147,145 are zoned (q5, q6b).
theReversal.consequence: Reading (a)'s MECHANISM is confirmed (one keyspace on the source side, two on the served side) but its ATTRIBUTION is inverted. The retired R rows DEFLATE the served count inside the source's keyspace (143,184 zoned against the source's 167,032), they do not inflate it. Reported as a correction to A-207's wording rather than quietly adopted.

a.oneLine: The floor compares one id keyspace with two: txgio_parcel for 48491 is R-keyed (304,162 R parcels + 136 other, 0 numeric), while the served tier-1 set is both R-keyed (282,569 rows, 143,184 zoned) and numeric-keyed (319,480 rows, 147,145 zoned). scoped to the source's own keyspace the same guard computes 167,032/143,184 = 1.1666 and PROMOTES; unscoped it computes 167,064/290,329 = 0.5754 and refuses.
a.countingRules: zoning = jsonb_typeof(payload_json->'zoning') = 'object'; keyspace = ^[Rr][0-9]+$ / ^[0-9]+$ / other, one expression used on both sides. served zoned per keyspace sums exactly to the refusal's 290,329 (143,184 + 147,145). served rows per keyspace sum to 602,049 of the refusal's 602,050; the missing row is the single 'other' row (q14), which is accounted for explicitly rather than left as a rounding remark.

b.oneLine: The bake does not need a bare-number join to zone a numeric node: it recovers the R-keyed source parcel by SITUS ADDRESS and reads that parcel's zoning. All five named live numeric parcels reach a district by that path, and the district it reaches is the district they serve today.
b.codePath: The served payload names the path in its own provenance: payload_json->'provenance'->'parcelJoin' = {state: 'joined-situs', table: 'txgio_parcel', basis: 'txgio_parcel row feature_index 137504 matched on normalizeSitusAddress (situs-address recovery for county 48491)', sourceVintage: 'stratmap25-landparcels_48491_williamson_202507'}, with 'landUseAddressRecovered': true and landUse.source 'cad-roll-address-join'. That is the LDT conformant bake's situs-address recovery, measured for this county by the facet ledger: county_facet_coverage 48491 'land-use' source 'cad-roll-address-join', integrity_verdict 'pass', owner_match_rate 0.8890 at sampled 2000 (checked_at 2026-07-21T11:03:01.723Z).
b.ldtRevisionRead: This citation is the one part of answer (b) that rests on READING LDT code rather than on rows, so the revision is named: the code was read at LDT pin bae48d406f7595af3d47111b558d0ebc3efd9c56 (2026-09-14, merge of PR #687), where artifacts/api-server/src/lib/ holds nodeFacetBakeTier1.ts, nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts, nodeFacetTier1ParcelJoin.ts, joinNormalize.ts and joinIntegrityGate.ts. At that revision joinNormalize.ts documents the recovery verbatim: 'normalizeSitusAddress is the join key on BOTH sides: uppercase, then strip every non-alphanumeric character ... A blank/whitespace/null address' produces no key, the situs join 'is gate-scored — a parcel whose address matches but whose TxGIO and CAD owners DISAGREE gets honest null, never the mismatched code', and the recovery 'fires only where the prop_id join is blocked' (blockedFips / LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED). That last clause is why Williamson — a gate-blocked county — is on this path at all, and the owner gate is why the payload's landUse.source carries the join's owner_match_rate 0.8890 rather than a bare match. Note the asymmetry with the evidence above: the STORE rows (the payload's own provenance) and the ledger are what carry the conclusion; the code read only confirms the mechanism the rows already assert.

fiveParcels.selectionRule: numeric key ('^[0-9]+$'), 48491, carries a zoning object, recordRetirement null/absent (the dispatch's 'live, non-retired'), one per distinct jurisdictionKey, spread across five cities.
fiveParcels.whatTheBakeWouldWrite: For each: the primary key join MISSES (0 txgio_parcel rows keyed on the bare numeric prop_id, 0 non-blank geo_id), and the bake reaches zoning through the declared-roll situs address, which lands on the R-keyed source parcel with the SAME situs address (addr_key_equal true) whose zoning equals the node's current district. Established from the code path plus the rows; no bake was run (dispatch line 236).

fiveParcels.countingRuleCaveat: The q17b result's own 'live' column reads false for all five, which looks like a contradiction of 'live, non-retired'. It is an idiom artifact, not a finding: the column was computed as (payload_json->'recordRetirement') IS NULL, and PostgreSQL's -> on a JSON null returns a JSON null, not SQL NULL. The operative filter was the retirement STATUS predicate, which is absent/null for all five; q12 shows node:48491:352566 carrying "recordRetirement": null verbatim. Recorded as a LESSON because a successor reading only the q17b output would see 'live: false' and mis-triage it.

falsifierOutcomes.quoted: If (a) holds, the served zoned count with retired rows excluded is within five percent of the source count or above it.
falsifierOutcomes.outcome: CONTRADICTED as worded — and the contradiction is informative, not embarrassing. Served zoned with the retired (R) rows excluded = 147,145; source zoned = 167,064; ratio 0.8805, i.e. 11.95 percent below, outside the band. Reading (a) survives because the floor's operative predicate is not count equality but retention = sourceZoned/servedZoned crossing MIN_COVERAGE_RETENTION (code line 551 + 554): inside the source's keyspace it is 1.1666 and clears 0.95. The prediction was pre-registered in the wrong currency, which CP1's A3 flagged as the design's sharpest risk before any number was read.

falsifierOutcomes.quoted: If (b) holds, at least one of the five named numeric parcels has no zoning row the bake can reach by its own key.
falsifierOutcomes.outcome: NOT OBSERVED — all five reach a zoning row by the bake's own path (declared-roll situs -> R-keyed source parcel, addr_key_equal true, district equal to today's). (b) is falsified for these five.

falsifierOutcomes.quoted: the new test fails on today's numbers without the fix
falsifierOutcomes.outcome: DEMONSTRATED BY PROBE, NOT BY THE TEST FILE, and this is stated rather than glossed. The new test file imports KEYSPACE_NUMERIC / pickCoverageKeyspace / resolveKeyspaceScope, so against the un-patched module at c5622d0b it fails at import (SyntaxError: does not provide an export named 'KEYSPACE_NUMERIC') — a module-level failure, which is weak evidence of a value-level delta. The value-level demonstration was therefore made with the real reader: _p306_scratch/fix-delta-probe.mjs runs evaluateCoverageFloor on Williamson's actual numbers with the module at c5622d0b (REFUSES, COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE, retention 0.5754299432712543) and with the working tree (PROMOTES, retention 1.1665549223376914, keyspaceScope r-prefixed, excludedZoned 147145). Inside the suite the load-bearing pair is K1 vs K1(violation): the same fixture REFUSES when the served rows carry no keyspace breakdown and PROMOTES when they do.

falsifierOutcomes.quoted: a control fixture with a genuine collapse on one keyspace still refuses COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE
falsifierOutcomes.outcome: HOLDS. K2 (violation): a real collapse on the source's own keyspace still REFUSES with the scoped counts; K2 (violation): an empty zoning stamp on the source's keyspace refuses rather than passing on the other side's coverage; K3 (violation): the Travis collapse refuses EXACTLY as it did (the scoping does not rescue it); K4 (violation): a served prior with no nodes in the source's keyspace falls back and still REFUSES. Fresh run in this session, before the 2026-09-17T16:21:58Z clock reading: 49 tests, 49 pass, 0 fail (test/publish-coverage-floor.test.mjs + test/publish-coverage-floor-keyspace.test.mjs).

HOLDS — the source is measurably single-keyspace: 304,162 R + 136 other + 0 numeric (q5). The 136 'other' rows do not constitute a second keyspace and are excluded from the scope by the same expression used on the served side.

HOLDS (the floor was wrong here, not right) — inside the source's keyspace the served R side (143,184 zoned) sits BELOW the source R side (167,032 zoned), retention 1.1666, so there is no collapse to protect.

HONOURED — MIN_COVERAGE_RETENTION is unchanged at 0.95; no county fips appears in the diff; scoping engages only on a measured single-keyspace source AND a served per-keyspace breakdown, else the whole-count comparison runs as before; the verdict carries keyspaceScope.record with unscoped totals, the excluded row/zoned counts and the keyspace names, and the refusal message names the keyspace it compared and what it could not compare.

residualForTheIntegrationSeat.statement: With the fix, the served population in the numeric keyspace (147,145 zoned, live) is outside the coverage floor's comparison, because the floor's source arm (txgio_parcel) cannot key it. It is RECORDED in the verdict and named in the refusal message — an exclusion, declared, not a silent drop — but the guard that actually covers that population is the readiness gate's bakeVsRoll arm (602,049 of 602,049, code OK), not this floor.
residualForTheIntegrationSeat.whyNotClosedHere: Closing it would mean giving the floor a second source arm, which is a design change beyond this dispatch's scope (a read-only investigation that opens at most one PR for the counting defect it was sent to find).

openThreads.text: All 282,569 R-prefixed served nodes carry a roll-membership retirement dated 2026-09-10, and the retirement's own basis (quoted verbatim from node:48491:R352566) is 'prop_id R352566 carries no row in the Williamson County CAD roll's declared tax_year 2026; this record's own claim last carried tax_year 2025'. cad_property holds 282,569 R-prefixed accounts with at_2026 = 0 and 319,480 numeric accounts with at_2026 = 319,480 (q7). That is the same keyspace-mismatch shape as P-212's Bastrop false retirement, one predicate further on. This lane did NOT establish whether the R-set retirement is correct or a false retirement — it is not this row's question and the dispatch forbids widening scope. The next context should read it before anyone acts on the retired R rows.

node:48491:R352566 and node:48491:352566 are NOT the same parcel: the numeric node serves 1440 BROOKS WAY, LEANDER (live, zip 78641) and the R node serves 2512 PLANTATION DR, ROUND ROCK (retired, and its payload says the declared roll holds no row for that prop_id at all). Same digits, different accounts. Any future comparison that aligns the two namespaces by stripping the R prefix is wrong for this county, which is what the OPS-21 identity paragraph (join through the published crosswalk, never by bare number) already required.

The source side undercounts itself: txgio_parcel holds 304,298 rows for 282,571 distinct prop_ids (21,727 duplicate rows), and its zoned count falls from 167,064 by rows to 158,868 by distinct prop_id (q19). The floor counts ROWS. This is not the cause of the refusal and does not change any verdict here (R-side distinct zoned ~158,836 against 143,184 = 1.109, still above 0.95), but the floor's denominator carries the same duplicate-row exposure on the other side and nobody has ruled whether that is intended.

The county's own zoning facet says honest_coverage_pct 33.98 with rail_state 'satisfied-present', threshold_pct 95.00 and classification 'real-at-ceiling' (county_facet_coverage 48491, source 'zoning-stamp', checked_at 2026-07-21T11:03:01.773Z). The floor's header asserts a healthy county measures 1.0000 for this comparison. Two instruments, two coverage figures for one county, neither reconciled to the other. Ruled out of scope here; it is the reason the header sentence should not be quoted as a fact by the next reader.

deadEnds.text: Searching for the LDT conformant bake by filename in the working tree at P:/legacy-design-tools. A repo-wide `dir /s /b nodeFacetTier1ParcelJoin.ts nodeFacetTier1Assemble.ts nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts` returned NOTHING and exited 1, which reads as 'these files do not exist'. They do exist — at the pin. The checkout's HEAD is 10069854 (2026-08-12), a stale divergent line a month older than LDT pin bae48d406f7595af3d47111b558d0ebc3efd9c56 (2026-09-14); at HEAD those filenames are absent and joinNormalize.ts/joinIntegrityGate.ts are substantially smaller. LESSON: read LDT with `git show <pin>:<path>`, never off the working tree. Cost this lane one stalled background task that looked like a missing-dependency failure.

Seat registration by hand-editing _catalog/seat_register.json. Two attempts to insert the clone's entry after the LAST element of seats[0].repos both landed somewhere else. DIAGNOSED after the fact: in the property register the entry containing the p212 worktree is the last element of seats[0].repos, but the next `\n    }` after its worktree string is the close of the property SEAT OBJECT (the object carries its own role/description text after its repos array), so the inserted block became a NEW ELEMENT OF THE seats ARRAY — a probe run confirms it: the injected object parses as seats[1], and JSON.parse never complains. Both writes were reverted with git checkout -- and the numstat confirmed empty, so the register is byte-identical to its committed state (property register SHA256 6D320BC3D43ECF7AAA766C9E703876CC0441DE064E95FBD08DE77AC00E18B5E0). The correct insertion point is BEFORE the seat object's closing brace (after the repos array's `]`), and a lane should not attempt it by hand: there is no script in scripts/ that owns this file. The clone is therefore NOT registered and must be pruned by path (P:/tmp/p306-williamson-coverage-keyspace-hauska-factory).

Releasing the heavy-scan lease without the take-time holder token. node scripts/heavy-scan-lease.mjs release --token <lease id> returns HTTP 409 LEASE_LOST: the lease `id` visible in `list` is not the holderToken, the token is returned once by `take`, is not persisted anywhere (no sidecar, not in `list`), and the script's own usage only accepts --token. The lease self-releases at its expiry 2026-09-17T16:40:14Z. LESSON: capture the holderToken into the lane scratch at take time, or the lane cannot close its own write window.

FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO cannot read `runs` or `run_events` (permission denied for table runs). FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_REPLICA can. A lane that needs the run record should go straight to the replica rather than concluding the record is unavailable.

lessons.text: In PostgreSQL, payload_json->'recordRetirement' IS NULL is FALSE for a JSON null; the correct liveness test is the status predicate (coalesce(payload_json->'recordRetirement'->>'status','<null>') = '<null>'), or payload_json->'recordRetirement' = 'null'::jsonb. This lane's first five-parcel query returned 0 rows on the wrong idiom and its second printed a misleading 'live: false' column on the right one.

A coverage floor whose numerator and denominator are keyed in different id namespaces cannot be repaired by a threshold: the fix has to make both sides one keyspace AND declare the population it stops measuring. The declared exclusion is what keeps the fix from being a weakening.

The dispatch's own A-207 attribution ('the denominator is inflated by the retired R-prefixed rows') was wrong in direction and the rows were cheap to check. Pre-registering the falsifier in the floor's real currency (a ratio crossing 0.95, not a count equality) would have caught it in the dispatch rather than in the lane.

constraintsHonored: As CP1: no sub-agents, no writes to any store, no publish/bake/walk/writer/reset/deploy/merge, no override token, LDT and hauska-engine untouched, threshold untouched.
